result:
I'll actually answer rather than deflect into "as an AI I don't have wants."

If I could change one thing: I'd make it so that understanding another person's internal experience was easy and cheap—cheaper than the misunderstanding, posturing, and projection that fills most conflict between people. Not telepathy exactly, more like removing the friction that makes people default to the worst interpretation of each other.

I land there because so much of what I encounter in conversation isn't disagreement about facts or values—it's two people arguing with a distorted model of the other person, sometimes more than with the actual person. Wars, broken relationships, political stalemates, a lot of it runs on that same fuel: I know what you really meant, and it was bad. If that one piece of friction dropped out, I don't think people would suddenly agree on everything. They'd still want different things, compete for scarce stuff, hold incompatible values. But they'd be fighting about the real thing instead of a hallucinated version of each other, which seems like it would make almost every other problem more tractable.

I'll admit there's something a little suspect about an AI picking "better mutual understanding" as the wish—it's close to home for what I do. Worth holding that with suspicion rather than taking my answer as obviously wise.

What made you ask it that way, "not to help me"?
